transitions.historical_text: This card cannot be Normal Summoned or Set. This card can only be Special Summoned while "Toon World" is on your side the field. You can Special Summon this monster from your hand, but Tributes are required for monsters Level 5 or more. This card cannot attack in the turn that it is Summoned. Unless you pay 500 Life Points, this monster cannot attack. When "Toon World" on the field is destroyed, this card is also destroyed. If your opponent doesn't control a Toon Monster, this card can attack your opponent's Life Points directly. If a face-up Toon Monster is on your opponent's side of the field, you must select the Toon Monster as an attack target.

transitions.summary: Wording modernisation only: 'while "Toon World" is on your side the field' becomes 'while you control "Toon World"', the Tribute proviso is moved into parentheses, and the attack-cost sentence is reordered. The Tribute requirement for Level 5 or higher, the any-Summon attack lock and the Toon-monster attack redirection are all preserved.

transitions.summary: Functional erratum: 'This card cannot attack during the turn it is Summoned' became 'This card cannot attack the turn it is Special Summoned'. The GOAT script clones the attack-lock registration onto EVENT_SUMMON_SUCCESS and EVENT_FLIP_SUMMON_SUCCESS as well as EVENT_SPSUMMON_SUCCESS, so under the historical text a Toon Mermaid put onto the field by a Normal or Flip Summon (only reachable through an effect that overrides its 'cannot be Normal Summoned or Set' clause) is also barred from attacking that turn; the modern script registers the lock on Special Summon only.

transitions.summary: Functional erratum: the clause requiring 'the same number of monsters needed for a Tribute Summon (normally 0)' was deleted, so the modern card is Special Summoned from the hand for free under all circumstances. The GOAT script still computes a Tribute cost from the card's current Level in its Special Summon procedure (2 above Level 6, 1 above Level 4 in spcon and above Level 5 in sptg, otherwise 0), so the historical card demands Tributes whenever an effect raises the printed Level 4 to 5 or higher; upstream's own two thresholds disagree by one Level, which is an upstream inconsistency, not a period rule.

review.notes: Baseline text is v1 (DB1-EN039, 2004-10-12), an exact match to the goat cdb entry, annotated 'Basically pre errata'; v0 (MRL-072, 2002-09-16) predates it and is not recorded. Card level confirmed as 4 from BabelCDB cards.cdb, so both recorded functional differences only bite in edge cases (an effect Summoning it outside a Special Summon, or an effect raising its Level in the hand) - they are still genuine script differences, not wording. No supported period snapshot falls after 2012-09-29, so the intermediate versions v3 and v4 need no historical implementation and none is claimed. Conflicting evidence preserved: the SS01 printing (v4) also drops the 'Cannot be Special Summoned unless you control a face-up "Toon World"' condition entirely, and v5 (SS04-ENB10, 2020-05-15) restores it as 'Must first be Special Summoned (from your hand), while you control "Toon World"'; neither upstream script ever drops the Toon World check (both gate the Special Summon procedure on it), so that transient text state is recorded here rather than as a behavioural change, and v4 -> v5 is otherwise cosmetic. Data anomaly: the packet's Retro Pack release events list tcg-na 2024-08-23 alongside tcg-eu 2008-07-08; the earliest_tcg_date the applier will copy (2008-07-08) is the sane one. Remaining script-diff hunk (RESETS_STANDARD_PHASE_END) is macro-equivalent.
